quarterly_data.signal: CFO Kevin Brady on Q3 2026 results: revenue was $716 million, up 8.5% year-over-year (nine months: $2.13 billion, up 16.9%); EBITDA margin of 24% (22.5% a year earlier) benefited from lower reimbursable costs; net income of $137.5 million increased 23.7%, growing faster than EBITDA mainly on higher interest income and a lower effective tax rate; year-to-date net income was $382.7 million versus $316 million, a 21.1% increase, and year-to-date diluted EPS $13.37 versus $10.64; net days sales outstanding was negative 66 days. On direct-service margins, he called performance 'very good' but said margins can be lumpy quarter to quarter (contract-signing timing and ASC 606 effects) and he does not see anything that would significantly disrupt margin performance in Q4.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $716 million (+8.5%); Q3 net income up 23.7%; year-to-date net income $382.7 million (up 21.1%); year-to-date diluted EPS $13.37 versus $10.64

quarterly_data.signal: CEO August Troendle: the business environment remained strong in Q3 2026, with high-quality RFP activity, strong initial award notifications and a good win rate; net new business awards (CFO: $873.4 million, up 10.6%) reached an all-time high, with last-12-month awards entering backlog of $3.02 billion, up 23.9%; CFO: ending backlog approximately $3.2 billion (+5.6%), of which approximately $1.99 billion is projected to convert to revenue in the next 12 months. Backlog cancellations were 'toward the higher end, but within kind of the range we'd expect' - 'not something to call out, but also not a help'; cancellations are now primarily product failure (products not living up to expectation, safety signals), with no real sign funding is a main driver. The total dollar value of pending opportunities is up nicely while RFP numbers are down some; most quarterly awards come from pre-backlog, entering backlog when a study starts operationally. For Q4: 'if things go right, it is going to be another record awards', and he expects another step up in trailing-12-month awards, depending on whether unusual cancellations occur.
quarterly_data.figure: net new business awards $873.4 million (all-time high); last-12-month awards $3.02 billion (+23.9%); approximately $1.99 billion of backlog projected to convert in the next 12 months

quarterly_data.signal: Medpace guidance on the call: CFO Kevin Brady - full-year 2026 revenue now expected at $2.835 billion-$2.855 billion (growth of 12%-12.8%) and EBITDA of $638 million-$652 million represents growth of 14.4%-16.9% over $557.7 million in 2025, with pass-through costs in Q4 expected 'kind of 40%-40.5%' of revenue, around where Q3 finished. CEO August Troendle: guidance for 2027 will come with Q4 reporting in February because the view of 2027 'has moved, and we expect it to continue to move'; 'we see no large disconnect between analyst consensus estimates and our current modeling of 2027' ('I'm not saying it's the same, but it didn't look drastically off'); things are improving month-to-month in increasing Medpace's 2027 revenue expectations, with Q4 awards and the Q4 cancellation pattern the key factors. CFO: a new significant expansion coming online in Cincinnati will add about $20 million of operating costs in 2027, 'some level of headwind in 2027 as we absorb the Cincinnati campus expansion'.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenue $2.835 billion-$2.855 billion; 2026 EBITDA $638 million-$652 million (growth 14.4%-16.9%); Q4 pass-throughs 40%-40.5%; Cincinnati expansion about $20 million of 2027 operating costs

quarterly_data.signal: CEO August Troendle on workforce: turnover 'looks very low' and has stayed low; there is no real change over the past year in salary, wage or benefit pressure - rates always increase some, but within expectations. CFO Kevin Brady: utilization 'continues to be in a good spot'; attrition rates are in a very good spot and, while headcount grows, revenue is growing faster at the moment.

CEO August Troendle on mix and clients: awards, notifications and to some extent RFPs have pivoted back toward traditional oncology, generally Medpace's largest area, with a little less metabolic demand - metabolic notifications and awards are down, but there are a lot of pending metabolic opportunities and quite a bit of metabolic work in RFPs again. Large pharma opportunities come from a limited number of providers and are often related to former biotech clients that were acquired, not direct outreach to win work at new large pharma clients. Medpace prefers fully full-service work and does front-end-only projects, but is 'not interested at all' in truly functional (FSP) work; he sees no meaningful increase in clients carving out biometrics. CFO Kevin Brady: top five and top 10 customers represent roughly 31% and 39% of last-12-month revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: top five customers roughly 31% and top 10 roughly 39% of last-12-month revenue

quarterly_data.signal: CEO August Troendle on win rate and market conditions: after recognising its win rate in 2025 was not as high as it would like, Medpace made meaningful process adjustments toward the end of 2025, which his assessment to date says have been very successful. Client decision timelines are moving faster than last year, with RFPs 'not being bid a thousand times' and clients wanting to move forward in the current time frame - 'a pretty normalized environment'. Medpace focuses on quality of deliverables rather than pricing, and 'some of the crazy approaches taken by some in the past few years have died out'. Over the last few years its growth profile dropped quite a bit, primarily from cancellation pressure.
